title: Three months solo with AI agents in Unreal: 11 tool sets, one real game, and what actually held up
author: KovatiDev
selftext:
Hi, I'm Bojan. I spent almost 20 years in film and real-time work, and this year I left a company I co-founded, which had reached seven figures in revenue, to work on one question: which AI pipelines survive contact with a real game?

I'm testing that on my own game, Colony: New Origins, solo for now. Along the way I've built free tools for Unreal, and the video is a two-minute tour of them. Here's what I've learned so far.



**What held up**

\- **Agents working from scripts.** Claude Opus 5.5 writes each vehicle as a Blender script from a concept sheet. I review it and give notes, it rebuilds, and scripted play tests check the result in Unreal. Changes go into the script, never the .blend file, so every version can be rebuilt.

\- **Keeping the shell of a generated mesh.** One Tripo buggy came back as 175 parts, with no UVs and faces missing, but the silhouette was right. We kept the shell, rebuilt everything that moves, and now you can drive it.

\- **Generating options early.** Should a stimpack be a sharp stab or a braced two-handed press? You can try ten versions in ten minutes, then bring in mocap once the design has settled.

\- **Temporary voices and faces.** A quest has no pacing until the lines are spoken, and this lets you hear a scene before anyone records it.



**What didn't**

\- **Quad retopology on generated meshes.** I got clean quads and a destroyed mesh, with the fine detail gone.

\- **Small print.** Warning signs and lettering come out as smears, even at 4K on a mesh with nearly half a million triangles. Retexture anything a player has to read.

\- **Fingers on the free local motion model.** It doesn't animate them, so hands need a different route.

\- **Treating the first result as finished.** That's where most slop comes from, in my experience, including my own.



**What I built because of all that**

I started from the idea that today's model is the worst one I'll ever use, so most of the effort went into the harness around the models.

\- **Providers are swappable.** A provider can run on your own GPU, on a rented GPU, or on a hosted service like Tripo, Meshy or ElevenLabs using your own account. They all sit behind the same interface, so a better model next month is a new provider rather than a rewrite.

\- **Costs come first.** On paid runs, you see the price before you spend anything.

\- **Every result is kept.** Each one is stored as a candidate with a record of the model, seed and inputs. Nothing gets overwritten, and re-running unchanged work costs nothing.

\- **Human edits win.** If you edit an asset by hand, the pipeline refuses to overwrite it.

\- **Replacing is cheap.** When the real asset arrives, swapping it in is just a reference change, because the game never knew the first one was generated.

\- **Agents get the same controls as people.** Every button is also a tool an agent can call through Unreal's MCP.



None of this replaces animators, actors or artists. It changes when you commit their time: after you've played the game and know what it is.



**What's free**

All of it is free to download right now, and 27 of the 41 plugins are open source, including all 16 agent toolsets. The rest are closed source but free, including four I plan to charge for later. Hosted services bill you directly. Later on, some advanced tools will be paid, and I'm also building a product for whole studios. It targets UE 5.8 on Windows, and parts of it are still developer preview, so expect rough edges.



**What I'd love to hear from you**

Which AI pipelines have actually held up in your projects, and which ones looked great until you tried to ship them?



\- Download the Hub, which installs the plugins (you add them to your account first): [https://kovati.dev/download](https://kovati.dev/download)

\- Source on GitHub: [https://github.com/AutomationForgeHQ](https://github.com/AutomationForgeHQ)

\- Devlogs and walkthroughs on YouTube: [https://www.youtube.com/@AutomationForgeByKovati](https://www.youtube.com/@AutomationForgeByKovati)

comments.body:
I'm Bojan, thanks for write up and plugin. this might be very useful. 

I'm working on building game, I don't have 20 years experience. I've been working for a year doing some sample projects (without ai, before that i was a software dev). Do you have any suggestions for someone in my position?

replies.author: KovatiDev
replies.body:
What is your background in software? And do you have any experience with any 3D whatsoever?

I suggest you check my tools, as they do come in with a lot of decisions made for you by default (you can obviously do things your way) but one of the ideas was that I “bake in” some knowledge and wisdom regarding workflows and pipelines. 

As for the thing you said “without ai”, I am not sure if you ment right now or you were referring to your previous work in software?
